title: Benedict XVI (2005–2013)
hook: a quiet theologian whose first encyclical was God is love

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Catechism: one book, four parts, numbered paragraphs. Your line was one summary. Which paragraph did you read? Today, a man who helped make that book, and then became pope. Day nine hundred thirty-one.

A new pope's first encyclical is watched closely. It's the first long letter he writes to the whole Church, and people read it for a program. This one came from a man who had spent his life as a professor and then as the Vatican's guardian of doctrine. Some expected rules. Its title, in Latin, was three words: Deus caritas est. God is love. It opens with a line from the first letter of John, and then it does something some readers did not expect from a strict theologian. It talks about eros, the love of desire, and about agape, the love that gives itself away, and it says the two belong together.
screen: `A FIRST LETTER, CLOSELY WATCHED.` → `SOME EXPECTED RULES.` → `DEUS CARITAS EST.`

segments.voice: His name was Joseph Ratzinger, and as pope he took the name Benedict. Four ways in. First, the scholar. He was a theologian before he was a bishop, a writer of books, more at home at a desk than on a balcony. He had worked on the Catechism you met yesterday, and for a long time he guarded Catholic teaching in Rome, which earned him critics as well as admirers. Second, the name. Benedict is the name of the monk of Nursia, whose rule shaped monasteries across Europe, and of Benedict the Fifteenth, a pope who pleaded for peace in a world war. Third, the letter. The first letter of John, in the Douay-Rheims, uses an older English word for love: "God is charity: and he that abideth in charity, abideth in God, and God in him." Charity there doesn't mean a donation. It's the Latin caritas, love itself. Benedict's letter starts there and then turns practical: if God is love, then the Church's care for the poor and the sick isn't a side activity. It belongs to what the Church is, as much as the sacraments and the preaching of the word. Fourth, what people disagree about. Some remember him as a brilliant, gentle teacher. Others remember the strict guardian of doctrine, or a papacy troubled by scandal. Both are part of the record. But when he wrote his first letter to the whole Church, he gave it a three-word title. And that brings the week to its end: from forgiving the gunman, through Assisi, World Youth Day, the Day of Pardon, the abuse crisis and the Catechism, to a pope whose first word to the Church was love.
screen: `JOSEPH RATZINGER, THE SCHOLAR.` · `THE NAME OF A MONK AND A PEACE POPE.` · `GOD IS CHARITY: LOVE ITSELF.` · `ADMIRED AND CRITICIZED.` · then, large: `GOD IS LOVE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: read 1 John 4, or begin with one verse of it. Settle, and breathe. Say the line slowly, in the old words: God is charity, and he that abideth in charity abideth in God. Then put a face on it. Who loved you when nothing was in it for them? A neighbor, a friend, a stranger who helped. Stay with that person for a while. If you pray, you can thank God for them. If you don't, simply be grateful. Later today, read the whole chapter; it's short. The bell holds the time.
Benedict the Sixteenth. Joseph Ratzinger, a theologian who became pope and whose first encyclical was Deus caritas est: God is love.
Your line: God is love. Today, do one act of charity in the old sense, love that costs you something, and don't mention it to anyone. Day nine hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Catholics read the first letter of John at Mass at various points in the year, and parishes and charities sometimes study Deus caritas est for its teaching that care for the poor belongs to the Church's own life.

fork.setup: you're a new pope, known as a strict guardian of doctrine. you have one first letter to the whole Church. what is it about?
options: God is love, and what that asks of the Church.
fork.reveal: he wrote Deus caritas est: God is love, joining eros and agape, and calling the Church's charity part of its very life.

original.note: Latin: God is love, from 1 John 4 in the Vulgate, and the title of Benedict XVI's first encyclical.

trapdoor: what you thought: charity means giving money.
what it means: in 1 John, charity is the old English for love itself: God is charity.
what a scholar hears: the Latin caritas behind the Douay-Rheims, and Benedict's letter holding eros and agape together.

notes: Claims rule: no dates spoken. Outline hook says 'shy theologian'; softened to 'quiet' and 'more at home at a desk than on a balcony', a characterization Keeper may cut.
Ratzinger's role on the Catechism (he chaired the commission that prepared it) and as Prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith ('for many years'): confirm.
Benedict's own explanation of the name (Benedict of Nursia and Benedict XV) comes from his first general audience; confirm.
Deus caritas est: confirm it discusses eros and agape as belonging together and that charity is part of the Church's nature alongside sacraments and the word.
